description: Composition variant of the pinned PULP apb_timer (the irq_o pulse endpoint profile) declared at 10 MHz and built with Verilator --timing.  The RTL schedules no delayed events, so this variant exists to prove the timed model build/link and the per-model phase path for an untimed CPU; no event-order claim is made from it.  It is a harness composition declaration, not an upstream synthesis rate.

resets.release: The timer count, compare and prescaler registers asynchronously reset on negedge HRESETn; release must satisfy HCLK recovery/removal timing.

interrupts.hold: Native equality output; not latched status. One source-clock pulse at prescaler equality, then count resets.
interrupts.clear: Automatic counter reset on the following HCLK edge; no acknowledge register.

semantics: Both selected source files, parameters APB_ADDR_WIDTH=12/TIMER_CNT=2 and all 11 top ports are pinned by the source lock and elaboration closure.

The top uses PADDR[4] to select one of two timers. Each timer uses PADDR[3:2] for count, control and compare at offsets 0,4,8. Timer 1 aliases at offsets 0x10,0x14,0x18; high address bits are ignored.
The timer module assigns PREADY=1 and PSLVERR=0. APB writes store whole PWDATA on PSEL/PENABLE/PWRITE; there is no PSTRB. Unmapped slot reads zero and writes have no register case arm.

Writing compare also resets count. Control bit 0 enables counting; control bits 5:3 select prescaler. IRQ bits [2*k] and [2*k+1] are overflow and compare equality outputs from timer k, not held status registers.
All state uses posedge HCLK and asynchronous active-low HRESETn.
verified: Verilator --lint-only succeeds on the two-file closure with 9 recorded nonfatal warnings; dependency replay reads exactly those two pinned files.
unknown: Host pulse capture/delivery width must be explicitly declared. CPU acceptance, first-handler serial lineage and ISR MMIO require actual native receipts; this profile alone grants none.
Only APB_ADDR_WIDTH=12/TIMER_CNT=2 is accepted; other parameterizations are not claimed.
